items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the general business law, in relation to providing notice of
certain scams when selling gift cards
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S145

SPONSOR: THOMAS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the general business law, in relation to providing
notice of certain scams when selling gift cards

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To require businesses to post notice alerting customers about gift card
scams. SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

  Section 1 amends section 396-i of the general business law by adding a
new subdivision 2-b. Subdivision 2-b, paragraph (a) states that no busi-
ness  or  store  can let individuals purchase gift cards unless a notice
alerting customers about gift card scams. Paragraph (b) states that  the
notice  can  be displayed two ways, with subparagraph (i) stating if the
business has an electronic paying system, the notice may be displayed on
the screen prior to finalizing the purchase and subparagraph (ii)  stat-
ing  if the business does not have a electronic screen, the notice shall
be posted in the location where the sale occurs.

  Section 2 is the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The number of scammers using gift cards as a mechanism to  obtain  money
is  steadily  growing.  According  to  a 2018 AARP report, 26 percent of
scammers used gift cards  as  their  main  way  to  con  consumers  into
payment,  which  was  an  increase  7 percent that used them in 2015(1).
These scams are often phone calls targeting consumers, particularly  the
elderly  and  immigrants,  stating  that they owe money where payment is
required by gift card. These individuals purchase the gift cards due  to
being  unaware they are being scammed and believe they will be penalized
if they do not comply.

The increasing amounts of these scams prompted Consumer Reports and  the
Public Service Commission to issue statements about the warning signs of
gift  card  scams(2).  Despite  these  public service announcements from
Consumer Reports and the Public Service Commission,  consumers  continue
to be taken advantage of by gift card scams.

This  bill  would  require  stores  where  gift cards are sold to post a
notice alerting customers to protect themselves from  gift  card  scams.
By requiring a warning message for consumers, it will reduce the success
rate  of  these scammers. The warning message will help all customers be
more aware of gift card scams, and will encourage  vulnerable  customers
to alert law enforcement if they believe they are being scammed.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2020:  S.7905 (Thomas)/A.9855 (Paulin) - Referred to Consumer Protection
Committee.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None noted to the State.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This  act  shall  take  effect  on the ninetieth day after it shall have
become a law.

Section 2 provides the effective date.

This bill would require stores where gift cards are sold to post a

By requiring a warning message for consumers, it will reduce the success
rate of these scammers. The warning message will help all customers be

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

A.9855, of 2020, referred to consumer affairs and protection / S.7905,

None.
